# Accessibility Service Overlay

Read another app's **live view hierarchy** through the platform accessibility channel, compute
something from it, then draw the answer back **on top of that same app** — without modifying it,
without root, and without a screenshot. The whole capture architecture of [[farely]] rests on this one
idea.

## Why it is a concept and not just an API

Three properties fall out of the choice, and they are what make it transferable:

- **The text arrives already parsed.** Nodes carry `text`, `contentDescription` and — with
  `flagReportViewIds` — stable view IDs. No image processing, microseconds instead of milliseconds.
  This is the whole argument in [[node-tree-read-before-ocr]].
- **The overlay is free.** A service that already holds the accessibility binding can attach a window
  of type `TYPE_ACCESSIBILITY_OVERLAY` with no additional user-granted permission. See
  [[accessibility-overlay-over-system-alert-window]].
- **The read is total.** Everything on screen is legible to the service, including screens the user
  would never consent to share. That is why the interesting engineering here is *restraint*, not
  reach.

## The restraint half

Farely narrows the channel at four points before any logic runs:

1. `accessibility_service_config.xml` restricts `packageNames` to four driver apps
   (`ee.mtakso.driver`, `com.ubercab.driver`, `taxi.android.driver`, `com.mytaxi.driver`). Nothing else
   on the phone is observed.
2. Events are debounced at 300 ms and limited to `WINDOW_CONTENT_CHANGED`, `WINDOW_STATE_CHANGED` and
   `NOTIFICATION_STATE_CHANGED`.
3. `MultiAppCoordinator.onScreen` sees the screen **before** the parser, and a `frozen` state
   short-circuits `process()` entirely — the identity-check freeze described on [[farely]].
4. Output is advisory only. The service never dispatches a gesture at a ride offer:
   [[never-automate-the-accept-tap]].

The ordering matters: freeze is checked *before* parse, so a frozen screen is never read, not merely
never acted on. The guarantee is still heuristic — it depends on a keyword list recognising the screen
— and that limit is recorded rather than smoothed over.

## Cost of the approach

- **Fragility to redesign.** Nodes are an implementation detail of someone else's app. Farely's answer
  is [[taught-selectors-over-guessed-labels]] — let the driver point at the real node instead of
  guessing labels per locale.
- **Terms-of-service exposure.** Reading and overlaying another company's driver app is documented as
  a ban risk in four separate places in the repo — an instance of
  [[privacy-documented-beside-the-feature]].
- **User trust cost.** Enabling an accessibility service is the single most powerful grant on Android,
  and the install guide says so.
